title: Customer case study
summary: A customer case study or testimonial film from a recorded interview with a client: situation, problem, why this product, what changed, signed-off numbers, 60 s to 3 min plus cut-downs.

notFor.when: the user wants the recording only cleaned up (silences, fillers, subtitles) in its own order, with no story built from it
a short native vertical ad (15-60 s) where a customer or creator talks to camera for TikTok, Reels or Shorts, not a recorded customer interview built into a story
only short vertical clips are wanted from the interview, with no case-study master
no customer was recorded: a launch film or ad that sells the product in its own voice
the film teaches how the product works with diagrams and a voice-over, not a customer's experience

alternatives.when: the approved paper edit keeps soundbites in recording order: the selects become the keep spans of a hand-made recording-edit request

the approved paper edit reorders soundbites (a footage timeline keeps source order; lower thirds and callouts work on it with timeline:edit add-overlay): a bespoke talking-head film plays each select by its source times

qa: Every soundbite keeps the customer's meaning in context: no answer spliced into a claim the customer did not make
Every number on screen or spoken matches the client's signed-off list, with its period and baseline
A result the client signed off as not typical carries an on-screen statement of what customers generally achieve
Any discount, free period, payment or partnership the client received is disclosed on screen
Lower thirds name the person and role as the client approved them; product screens are the real product

intake.ask: Has every person on camera signed a release that covers this film, its cut-downs, the platforms and the period of use?
intake.why: Without a release the film cannot be published; the licence text goes into the recording-edit request's source.rights

intake.ask: Who at the client approves the story cut and the numbers, and which figures, with period and baseline, are they willing to show?
intake.why: Every number on screen needs the client's sign-off and its substantiation; FTC 16 CFR 255.2

intake.ask: Did the client receive anything for taking part or as a customer that viewers would not expect: discount, free months, payment, partnership?
intake.why: A material connection must be disclosed clearly; FTC 16 CFR 255.5

intake.ask: Is the client's result typical of what customers generally achieve?
intake.why: If not, the film states what customers can generally expect, with substantiation; FTC 16 CFR 255.2(b)
intake.default: Not known to be typical: ask the user for the generally expected result before any number goes on screen

intake.ask: How many cameras, and what B-roll or product access exists (customer site footage, a test account for real screens)?
intake.why: Two cameras add multicam; B-roll and real screens cover cuts and carry the proof
intake.default: One camera; B-roll only from supplied footage via media:broll; real screens recorded with capture:app

intake.ask: Which lengths: one master and how many cut-downs, for which platforms?
intake.why: The master and cut-downs need separate selects and approvals
intake.default: One 90-120 s landscape master and 2-3 vertical cut-downs of 15-45 s through shorts-from-long

profiles.note: Length band is a house rule, starting point. Upload in the recorded frame rate, MP4 fast start, AAC 48 kHz; offer a clean render plus SRT (YouTube upload settings help).
LinkedIn allows 3 s to 15 min and 1:2.4 to 2.4:1; closed captions only as an SRT attached on desktop before posting. The length band is a house rule, starting point.
Case-study page or sales deck embed. Length band is a house rule, starting point; no source opened states one.

starter.note: Number callouts for a signed-off figure (odometer), a before/after metric pair and a payoff stat card; clean sentence captions for interview speech. type-lower-third names each speaker.

variants.title: Two-camera interview
variants.changes: Add multicam to --goal with --cameras <files>; multicam:sync then multicam:angles; a cut to the second angle hides a jump inside an answer. The paper edit still decides the order.

variants.title: Short testimonial
variants.changes: 15-45 s cut-down of a case-study master: one problem, one change, one signed-off number. Run as shorts-from-long on the same source project, with the same release and sign-off. A short ad cut for the feed goes to ugc-ad.

variants.title: Several people from the client
variants.changes: Diarise (--speakers N); one person carries the arc, the others answer one beat each; each needs a release and a lower third. Separate recordings cannot share one reviewed recording edit: use the talking-head film route.
